name: Merge PDF
purpose: Combine several PDFs into one file, in the exact order you choose.
short: Drag files into order, then merge them into a single PDF.

privacyNote: Each PDF is read with the File API and copied page by page using PDF-lib inside this tab. No file, filename or byte count is transmitted.
steps: Choose two or more PDFs. They are read locally and their page counts appear.
Reorder the list — drag the handle, or focus a row and use the arrow buttons.
Press Merge. PDF-lib copies every page into a new document in list order.
Download the merged file, or reset to release the buffers.

example.title: Combining a signed contract, an appendix and a cover sheet
example.body: Add the cover sheet first, the signed contract second and the appendix last. The list order is the page order, so no post-merge page shuffling is needed. The merged file keeps each source page at its original size, including mixed A4 and Letter documents.

does: Unlimited file count, limited only by available tab memory
Drag-and-drop reordering with keyboard move up / move down controls
Per-file page counts shown before you commit
Encrypted PDFs are reported instead of silently skipped
doesnt: Encrypted PDFs must be unlocked in a desktop reader first — this tool will not guess a password.
Form field values are preserved only when the source documents are unencrypted and standard AcroForm.
Very large jobs (hundreds of megabytes) can exhaust tab memory; the tool warns before starting.

faq.q: Are my files uploaded to a server?
faq.a: No. The merge runs in the tab with PDF-lib. You can confirm it yourself: open DevTools, switch to the Network tab, and merge a file — no request carrying file data appears.

faq.q: Why does an encrypted PDF fail?
faq.a: An encrypted PDF stores its page tree behind an encryption dictionary. Decrypting requires the password, and this tool has no password field, so it reports the file as unsupported rather than producing a corrupt output.

faq.q: Does merging reduce quality?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied as page objects, not re-rendered, so text stays selectable and images keep their original encoding.

name: Split PDF

Download the ZIP, or download individual parts.

faq.q: Can I split by bookmarks or a table of contents?
faq.a: Not currently. Bookmark outlines vary a lot between producers; ranges are predictable and verifiable, so they are the only split mode shipped.

faq.q: What happens to annotations?
faq.a: Page annotations travel with their page, because the page object is copied intact. Document-level attachments are not carried over.

faq.q: Is the ZIP created locally?
faq.a: Yes. JSZip assembles the archive in the tab from Blobs that already exist in memory.

Type the pages you want, for example 2, 5-7, 11.
Check the selected-page count.
Extract and download.

faq.q: Does extraction re-compress images?
faq.a: No. Pages are copied as objects, so image streams are untouched.

faq.q: Can I extract pages in a different order?
faq.a: Yes — the order you type is the order written, so 5, 2, 9 produces a document in that sequence.

faq.q: Why is my signature now invalid?
faq.a: A digital signature covers the exact bytes of the original file. Any page-tree change produces a new document, so the old signature no longer matches.

faq.a: No. Only the page dictionary changes, so text and images are byte-identical to the source.

faq.q: Can I rotate just page 3?
faq.a: Yes. Enter 3 in the page field and leave the rest alone.

faq.q: Why does my viewer ignore the rotation?
faq.a: A few legacy viewers ignore /Rotate. Modern browsers, Preview and Acrobat all honour it.

faq.q: Can I delete pages here?

faq.q: Do transparent PNGs keep transparency?
faq.a: PDF pages are opaque. Transparent areas are composited onto white, which is what most printers assume anyway.

faq.q: What quality setting should I use?
faq.a: 0.85 is a good default for photos. Use 0.95 for text screenshots, where JPEG artefacts are most visible.

faq.q: Can I mix portrait and landscape?
faq.a: Yes, choose “Fit to image” so each page takes the orientation of its image.

faq.q: Why is my scanned PDF slow to render?

faq.q: Is the text layer preserved in the image?
faq.a: No — raster export produces pixels. Use PDF Text Extractor when you need the characters.

faq.q: Can this tool read scanned documents?
faq.a: No. Text extraction reads an existing text layer. Recognising glyphs in an image is OCR, which is a different and much heavier operation.

faq.q: Why is the order of lines odd in a two-column paper?
faq.a: PDF stores text in drawing order, not reading order. Multi-column documents often need manual reordering after extraction.

faq.q: Are ligatures preserved?
faq.a: PDF.js maps common ligatures to their component characters. Unusual embedded fonts may produce replacement characters.

faq.q: Why does the Producer field keep coming back?
faq.a: Some libraries re-add a Producer value when saving. This tool writes an empty string for removed fields, which most viewers display as blank.

faq.q: Is the original file modified?
faq.a: Never. You get a new download; the source file on your disk is only read.

faq.q: Is GPS always present?
